claims.statement: SSHConnectionPreparation resolves ordered jumps and target in a cancellable detached task, applies strict Known Hosts or live challenges, and carries accessHostIDs, accessCheck and beforeConnect wake hooks; authenticated opening checks access and wake before route opening.

A configured proxy is attributed to its owning route host and is not a Journey endpoint: proxy connection and authentication remain on Local or the preceding SSH host, while only the next host SSH connection advances route progress.

Routed sockets authenticate ordered jumps through direct-tcpip bridges. Prepared startup executes backend control before terminal admission, supporting MaxSessions=1. The tmux dialect requires 3.3+, exact session/creation/PID/ownership matching, safe quoting, non-evicting attach and guarded TERMIND_ENDED termination; opt-in wire tests check resize, detach/restore and transport loss without startup replay.

Host-key authorization treats an external MD5 constraint only as an additional handshake constraint: a matching expected identity bypasses interaction, a conflicting known-host set still rejects, and an unknown identity requires an authorizer or fails closed.

Persistent Known Hosts trust is independent of Host records, while a Continue Once approval stays only in the live controller; persistent approval saves the key before resuming and disconnect rejects a pending decision and clears temporary keys.

SSHSecret shares and zeroizes owned buffers; copies clear target/proxy/jump secrets without clearing routing/provenance. Forbidden interaction turns target/jump Security Keys into interactionRequired and retries resolve saved credentials afresh.

SSHConnection serializes libssh2 calls through SSHConnectionWorker; worker cleanup increments a generation, cancels timers, fails commands, closes channel owners and the authenticated transport, preventing stale socket/timer work from affecting a retired connection.

Mobile cold launch retires legacy defaults and loads eligible restoration descriptors from a separate versioned store, without live workspaces, transports or history attempts until selection; recently-closed records remain process-local.

Telnet uses an independent direct-or-proxied TCP transport with generation-guarded callbacks, incremental Telnet negotiation and charset conversion, and consumes an automated password once; it is not an SSH trust, jump-host, or SFTP transport.

On desktop TermindApp shares one AppModel across scenes but constructs a WindowModel for each window; AppModel holds app-wide host services including an AgentHostServices resolver, authentication registry, connection pool and background-command owner, distinct from window-owned workspace sessions.

Agent host listing exposes public Vault metadata and temporary pane targets without credentials; temporary SSH configuration comes from a live desktop pane, and resolution fails when a temporary pane-backed target no longer exists.

Agent SSH authentication collects missing proxy and host credentials in route order before connecting; the attempt handles host-key and keyboard-interactive challenges during handshake, with permanent host-key trust allowed only for saved Hosts and one-shot approval held in the authentication context.

Overlapping Agent connections to the same host share a temporary authentication context and pending configuration/open; cancelling the last waiter cancels its prompt, stale generations cannot erase newer answers, and successful authentication clears staged secrets so unrelated later connections cannot reuse custom credentials.

AgentConnectionPool reuses an authenticated Host-ID-keyed connection across tools and runs according to a route fingerprint built without Keychain reads; route changes invalidate reuse, concurrent misses join an opening, and late cancelled openings are disconnected instead of committed.

The Agent pool multiplexes exec and primary SFTP over its own SSH connection, can obtain auxiliary or sibling SFTP channels, exempts active exec/SFTP leases from idle sweeping, and disconnects on host deletion or explicit app shutdown.

ssh_exec uses a non-PTY command channel with safe-command parallelism and approval for unproven commands; its deadline includes connection, returning connecting without starting a command if setup is still pending, or handing a running command to a background handle while retaining the pooled connection; only a pre-channel connection failure can be retried.

Desktop Quit saves theme edits and may veto unsaved themes or pending uploads, not open workspaces. Idempotent approved shutdown fences Assistant admission, retires windows and drains preparations/conversations, MCP and SFTP before closing Agent commands, pool and Tailscale; native reply occurs once after cleanup or three seconds.

All-scenes background starts resumable checkpoint suspension immediately and a UIKit task for remaining work. Expiration suspends ordinary flows, stops forwarding, pauses transfers and cancels Assistant; drains precede Agent command/pool closure. Foreground resumes recorded intent and preserves healthy ordinary SSH before expiration.

For an Agent connection through a proxy whose saved password identity is missing, the authentication card retains the proxy-configured username while clearing the unavailable identity selection; an unsaved proxy answer changes only the attempt, while a saved answer persists proxy identity and username to the host store.

When Agent authentication requires an identity followed by a protected-key passphrase, the passphrase response merges into the staged identity submission instead of replacing it, preserving any password fallback for that connection.

Native desktop window close uses a separate veto from Quit and disconnects only its owning window on actual closure while preserving managed sessions and recovery references; metrics policy can keep the app alive after the last window closes.

A workspace trust approval resumes the pending live host-key handshake rather than opening a separate discovery connection; the feature pauses recovery while waiting and disconnect clears pending decisions.

Desktop terminal connection preparation is prompt-first rather than exclusively SSHConnectionPreparation-based: SSHSessionModel resolves per-attempt staged proxy, host, key/passphrase and username requirements, builds the target and jump configuration from the host store, and routes credential errors to the failing hop or proxy before retrying.

Desktop attempt guards reject stale PTY installs/callbacks and disconnect failed installs. Explicit close deduplicates owned references for ownership-checked best-effort termination without failure UI; ordinary errors continue and permit local closure without confirming end, but cancellation or changed generation denies closure. Ownership snapshots reject stale removal; passive teardown preserves sessions and managed exit requires verified successful end.

Desktop AppModel.open configures per-window history callbacks, optimistic terminal status and workspace creation; HostLibraryModel aggregates per-connection status so an online sibling wins over failed or closed panes.

Desktop connection history is recorded when a saved-host pane opens, not when authentication succeeds, and is ended when the pane closes; source device identity, kind, latest-event recents and local-only filtering do not depend on a successful transport.

Mobile records saved-Host history and publishes live objects before connecting, persists eligible descriptors rather than transports/commands, reuses live objects on selection, keeps external links transient and ends history on authorized close.

Saved-host SSH/SFTP history records stable device/start/end identity; synchronized device names do not rewrite events. Cross-device timeline and local deduplicated Welcome recents are separate, with retained limit 250 and desktop/mobile display limits 100/50.

ConnectionHistoryModel trims the global history to 250 attempts on initialization and insertion, and reports repository failures as storageError rather than returning a successfully recorded event; local recents exclude records without the current stable source-device ID.

Mobile deletes malformed or valid legacy workspace/recently-closed defaults without migration, preserving unrelated settings. Separate mobile.restorableWorkspaces.v1 validates version and unique IDs and blocks saves after corrupt load.
All-scenes background pauses synchronization, metrics, outbox and external-edit monitoring; active foreground ends the task, rechecks edits, resumes recorded workspace intent and reconciles services.

Mobile reconciliation hands orphaned live objects to an active scene without reconnect or new history while persisting descriptor ownership; disconnect preserves ownership and late discard targets originating handed-off workspaces.

Mobile activity recovery validates version/source/Host/kind, publishes a new workspace before authentication and deduplicates deliveries. Retained payloads may restore same-Host SSH references, but URLs exclude ownership and commands; rebuild requires selection and invalid or ID-only old links cannot guess connections.
Mobile in-process reopen constructs fresh runtime from intent without replaying one-shot commands or initial paths; selection of an already-live workspace returns that object without retry.

Mobile plain SSH exit closes locally; managed exit needs zero status and confirmed absence. ResumableTerminalClient delegates to Mosh/ET engines: fresh startup bootstraps SSH while checkpoint restoration skips startup replay; suspension freezes writes and drains sends, resume reapplies viewport/integration, and failure rolls back. Mosh stopped drains final output, ET sessionEnded waits for output drain; silence/disconnect/EOF alone are not end. Ended emits once. Missing mobile checkpoints fail visibly; managed references permit selection over fresh transport without replay.

When SSHConnectionWorker loses its last reference it performs serialized cleanup inline if already on its connection queue and otherwise synchronously on that queue, avoiding self-deadlock while retiring transport; lifecycle tests exercise both release contexts.

SSH Security Key credentials resolve from Vault metadata for both destination and jump hosts without loading private key material from Keychain, and interactive SSH connection requests supply a Security Key signing callback.

Cancelling detached SSHConnectionPreparation prevents a resolved configuration from escaping with live secrets, and partial route resolution clears collected credentials and proxy passwords on failure or cancellation.
Cancelling SSH opening interrupts socket/authentication, wakes keyboard-interactive or Security Key signing and ignores late responses while serialized opening cleanup runs.

Both platforms prioritize explicit commands over current startup snippets; plain-shell startup submits when ready, managed creation passes commands into backend startup, and attachment clears pending commands without replay. Disconnect discards pending commands.

Desktop saved-host opening dispatches to a window pane starting on mount or retry; mobile resolves one-shot preparation with per-attempt trust/authentication callbacks before PTY or SFTP opening, while Agent connections use app-owned authentication and pooling.

PTY close preserves transport for live SFTP siblings or explicit control retention, not pending exec CLOSE. Optional tmux sizing activation requires focus, validated client, synchronized resize, runtime control and concurrent capacity; blur/input/detach/replacement invalidate stale requests, ordinary resize does not repeatedly activate and failure neither injects keys nor disconnects.
SFTP drivers retain their queue-confined SSH worker through asynchronous cleanup without an owner-to-driver retain cycle.
PTY worker deinitialization cleans up inline on its own serial queue and synchronously enters it only from other queues, avoiding reentrant sync deadlock while serializing teardown.

Desktop SSH and SFTP share synchronous controller authentication continuation with route/library/temporary host lookup and trimmed nonempty username validation. Identity submissions stage and resume before optional model-owned saving; proxy submissions save before staging and use the entered username; protected-key passphrases merge through passphraseSubmission. Only successful continuation connects, failed saves do not start another attempt, and callbacks are never retained.

Controller tokens reject stale progress and teardown precedes retry. Managed coordination defaults disabled with tmux/Ask, supports create/attach/plain/retry, confirms creation ownership and validates recovery; missing sessions require selection and uncertain creates reuse tokens only for identical intent. The service registers tmux, Zellij, zmx and herdr dialects; unknown backends fail unsupported.
